StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single with on_stack overridden to `pass` -- the census's wrong-reasoning class. DORMANT with a caveat that is NOT true of the other 14: Hex's Amount IS read -- it is the Hexed affliction's amount (`CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, base.Amount)`, HexPower.cs:79, vs `CardCmd.afflict(card, HexedAffliction, self.amount)`, powers.py:3209) -- so a second application would afflict LATER cards at 2 in the game and at 1 in the sim. It stays dormant only because the sole applier, monsters/glory/knights.py:119-120, applies it once and KNIGHTS_ELITE fields exactly one Spectral Knight (knights.py:129-131). Trigger: a second Spectral Knight or a second Hex application. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

TryModifyKeywordsInCombat.rationale: C# grants Ethereal through the keyword-modifier chain, gated on the card carrying the Hexed affliction, so the grant is live-computed and "when this power is removed, it stops contributing here automatically, so any Ethereal from another source (e.g. MusicBox) is left untouched" (HexPower.cs:21-25). The sim has no keyword-modifier hook, so it writes `card.is_ethereal` directly and stashes the previous value in `card._hex_prev_ethereal` (powers.py:3210-3211), restoring it on removal (powers.py:3238) -- which reproduces the "leave other sources untouched" property by save/restore instead of by non-contribution, and the sim's own docstring (powers.py:3195-3197) says exactly that. Observably identical for one Hex; it would diverge if a second source toggled Ethereal DURING the Hex, because the stashed value would then be stale. No ported source does (the sim's other Ethereal writers are card-static), so this is a deliberate-divergence with the mechanism named rather than a gap. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# afflicts every card in `PlayerCombatState.AllCards` via `Afflict`, which itself tests `card.Affliction == null` (HexPower.cs:39-45, 75-81); the sim's __init__ walks `owner.all_cards` with the same `card.affliction is None` test (powers.py:3221-3223). The __init__-for-AfterApplied substitution is the same mechanism as illusion's and dampen's. The `all_cards`-omits-Play concern does NOT bite: Hex is applied by the Magi/Spectral Knight's move on the enemy turn, and the sim's Play limbo only exists between combat.py:433 and combat.py:498 inside a player card play.

AfterCardEnteredCombat.rationale: HexPower.cs:47-53 afflicts any newly-entering card owned by the owner's player; powers.py:3225-3227 does the same with the same `card.affliction is None` test inside `_afflict`. The `card.Owner == base.Owner.Player` test is a single-player tautology.

AfterDeath.rationale: `!wasRemovalPrevented && creature == base.Applier` (HexPower.cs:57) maps to `if creature is self.applier: self._expire()` (powers.py:3230-3231). This is one of the four sim sites that READ `self.applier`, and it is right -- the applier IS threaded here, because monsters/glory/knights.py:120 passes `applier=self`. Worth contrasting with the enemy self-buffs in this half that omit it.

AfterRemoved.rationale: C# sweeps `PlayerCombatState.AllCards` and clears every Hexed affliction (HexPower.cs:63-73); the sim sweeps `owner.all_cards` and additionally restores `is_ethereal` from the stash. The `all_cards`-omits-Play risk IS real here -- unlike AfterApplied, this sweep runs when the APPLIER dies, which normally happens inside a player card play, i.e. exactly when a card is in the sim's Play limbo -- so it was **EXECUTED** rather than argued: a KNIGHTS_ELITE combat, Hex 1 applied by the Spectral Knight (all five hand cards come back ethereal with a Hexed affliction), then the knight killed by a Strike played from that hand -- and the played card comes out with `ethereal = False`, `affliction = None`, in the discard pile, exactly like the four cards that never left hand. The sweep reaches it. Recorded as checked because the hypothesis was that it would not.

guards.rationale: Single-player tautology; omitted by the sim.

guards.what: HexPower.cs:32 `!(card.Affliction is Hexed)` -> false in the keyword modifier
guards.rationale: The sim has no per-query gate because it writes the flag instead of contributing to a chain; the affliction is still the thing that decides which cards get the flag (powers.py:3209's `CardCmd.afflict(...) is not None` guards the write). Folded into the TryModifyKeywordsInCombat mechanism.

guards.what: Cards that already carry a DIFFERENT affliction are skipped
guards.rationale: `card.Affliction == null` on both sides (HexPower.cs:77, powers.py:3222/3226), so a card already Entangled or Ringing is never Hexed. This is the inverse of the tangled-power gap the main report records (section 4 item 13), where the sim ADDED an `Affliction == null` test C# does not have -- here C# has it and the sim matches. Worth recording so the two are not conflated.
